pl-l2d32c1-d1e108.summary: Asks how original sin, the defect of concupiscence, is remitted in baptism when concupiscence remains afterward; it seems either original sin is not concupiscence or it is not remitted.

pl-l2d32c1-d1e111.summary: Cites Augustine: carnal concupiscence remains in this body of death, whose desires we are commanded not to obey, though it lessens daily in those who advance and are continent.

pl-l2d32c1-d1e116.summary: Answers that concupiscence remains after baptism but does not rule as before; baptismal grace mitigates and diminishes it so that it cannot dominate unless one gives strength to the enemy by following desires. It does not remain as guilt, being not imputed as sin but only punishment; before baptism it is punishment and fault.
claims: After baptism concupiscence is punishment, not fault.

pl-l2d32c1-d1e120.summary: Concludes that original sin is remitted in baptism for two reasons: its defect is weakened so it does not reign unless consent strengthens it, and its guilt is loosed.
claims: Remission weakens concupiscence and looses its guilt.

pl-l2d32c1-d1e123.summary: Cites De baptismo parvulorum: baptismal grace crucifies the old man not so that innate concupiscence vanishes in living flesh, but so that it does not harm the dead what was in the born; the baptized must fight it with God's help; all evil done, said, or thought is abolished, but concupiscence, its bond of guilt loosed, remains for combat. So it is remitted because its guilt is abolished.
claims: Concupiscence remains for combat after its guilt is loosed.

pl-l2d32c1-d1e126.summary: Cites Augustine that baptism also weakens concupiscence: the law of the flesh remains in the reborn not as unremitted, but as overcome and slain, unless revived by illicit consent and restored to its reign. So it is remitted also because it is weakened.
claims: Concupiscence is overcome in the reborn unless revived by consent.

pl-l2d32c1-d1e131.summary: States that Scripture teaches this mode of remission by many more testimonies.

pl-l2d32c1-d1e134.summary: Cites Contra Iulianum: the law in the members is a defect of flesh from the punishment of sin; it is remitted by spiritual regeneration, its guilt loosed by the sacrament, and remains in mortal flesh, producing desires against which the faithful fight.
claims: Concupiscence is remitted in guilt and remains in operation.

pl-l2d32c1-d1e137.summary: Cites a sermon: by baptismal grace the guilt of concupiscence you were born with is loosed, along with whatever you consented to in thought, word, or deed.
claims: Baptism looses inborn and consented guilt.

pl-l2d32c1-d1e141.summary: Cites De nuptiis et concupiscentia: though concupiscence is not counted as sin in the regenerate, every child born is bound by original sin.
claims: Children of the regenerate are born with original sin.

pl-l2d32c1-d1e144.summary: Cites Augustine: concupiscence is remitted in baptism not so that it is not, but so that it is not imputed as sin; not having sin means not being guilty of it; as other sins like homicide pass in act and remain in guilt, concupiscence passes in guilt and remains in act.
claims: Concupiscence passes in guilt and remains in act.

pl-l2d32c1-d1e149.summary: Concludes that this shows how original sin is remitted in baptism.

pl-l2d32c1.summary: Asks how original sin is remitted in baptism when concupiscence remains afterward; it seems either original sin is not concupiscence or it is not remitted. Lombard answers that concupiscence remains but no longer rules; it is weakened by baptismal grace, and its guilt is dissolved, so after baptism it is only punishment, not fault. Original sin is remitted in two ways: the defect is weakened so it does not reign without consent, and its guilt is loosed. Augustine: concupiscence is remitted not so that it is not, but so that it is not imputed as sin; as other sins pass in act and remain in guilt, concupiscence passes in guilt and remains in act.
claims: After baptism concupiscence no longer reigns unless consent restores its power.
After baptism concupiscence is punishment only, not fault.
Original sin is remitted by weakening concupiscence and loosing its guilt.
Concupiscence passes in guilt and remains in act.
